The solver application in system/controlDict is rhoCentralFoam.
The thermophysical model in constant/thermophysicalProperties is hePsiThermo with equationOfState set to perfectGas and transport set to sutherland.
The working fluid is air, treated as a perfect gas.
The mesh is 2D in the xy-plane, extruded exactly one cell in the z-direction, and the frontAndBack boundary patch is set to type empty.
The computational domain is a rectangular region. The nozzle is not modeled; the inlet boundary represents the flat nozzle-exit plane where the flow is already at Mach 2.0.
The inlet face is a flat segment on the left boundary of the rectangle, centered vertically, with a height h_jet of 0.02 m. The inlet does not span the full height of the domain.
Two solid-wall segments are placed on the left boundary directly above and below the inlet face, representing the nozzle-exit lip. These are the only solid walls in the entire domain.
The top boundary, the bottom boundary, and the right (downstream) boundary of the rectangular domain are all far-field boundaries.
The inlet boundary condition is fixedValue for all three fields: U is (686 0 0) m/s, p is 101325 Pa, T is 300 K.
The far-field and downstream-outlet boundary conditions are waveTransmissive for p and T, and zeroGradient for U.
The wall boundary condition is noSlip.
The initial condition at t = 0 is uniform throughout the domain: U is (0 0 0) m/s, p is 101325 Pa, T is 300 K.
The domain height H_domain is chosen to be approximately 5 to 10 times h_jet (for example, 0.2 m), and the domain length from the left boundary to the right boundary is chosen large enough for the jet to expand and form shock-diamond structures before reaching the downstream boundary (for example, 0.4 m).
The z-extrusion thickness is arbitrary, for example 0.001 m, and is used only to satisfy the 3D mesh requirement of the solver.
The solver uses central spatial differencing and a second-order time-discretization scheme. There is no PIMPLE pressure-velocity loop, no separately solved pressure equation, and no momentumPredictor or nOuterCorrectors block in fvSolution.
